clues: The Greek physician Aretaeus of Cappadocia wrote the earliest known medical description of the condition in the 2nd century AD, using the term koiliakos, coming from the Greek word for 'abdominal'
This disease is characterized by three classic histological features: increased intraepithelial lymphocytes, crypt hyperplasia, and villous atrophy

During WWII, wheat shipments to the Netherlands were cut off by blockades. A Dutch pediatrician noted that children with this disease miraculously got better during this time, which led to the discovery of the causal proteins that trigger the immune response
The first clinical description of this disease was published in 1761 by an Italian Giovanni Battista Morgagni. This description was known as Morgagni's sign and later Courvoisier's law or sign
Several notable public figures have been diagnosed with this disease including Alex Trebek, long standing Jeopardy! host. In November, some will put up purple ribbons for this disease.
In part due to late presentations, this disease has a high mortality rate. Symptoms might include jaundice, back pain, or the development of type 2 diabetes

Hippocrates described patients with behavior consistent with this disease. He believed it was caused by an overbalance of fire over water and advised patients to eat fish instead of meat and participate in heavy physical movement

In 1937, physician Charles Bradley gave benzedrine to children with headaches after spinal taps which inadvertently treated this condition. This was the foundation for modern day treatments of this disease, which is still predominantly diagnosed in childhood
This disorder involves dysregulation of dopamine and norepinephrine signaling, particularly in areas controlling attention and motivation
In the early 20th century, syphilis tests used bovine heart extracts to spot antibodies. Doctors noticed that people with this disease gave a 'false positive' on these tests without having syphilis

Historians and medical sleuths suggest that Queen Anne may have suffered from this disease. Despite 17 pregnancies, none of her children survived into adulthood leaving her without a direct heir, ending the reign of the Stuart Dynasty over England, Scotland, and Ireland in 1714
Although some patients with antibodies are asymptomatic, some may develop a catastrophic version of this disease with rapid, widespread clotting, multiorgan failure, and a mortality rate of 30-50%

The origins of this disease are thought to have been zoonotic, potentially evolving from the animal virus Rinderpest (a disease found in cattle, bison, and other hooved animals). The first clear written account of this disease appeared in the 9th century by Persian physician Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Razi

Do you know how 'fifth disease' got its name? In that numbered naming system, this disease was previously called the 'first disease' and causes a unique immune amnesia where individuals infected by this disease lose pre-existing immune memory cells, removing prior immunity built up from past illnesses and vaccinations
Because a single person with this disease can infect 12-18 unprotected individuals, vaccine hesitancy has increased case rates in the United States
